lean.plain: Find-Any round bound for large domains
lean.annotation: This theorem gives the new algorithm's upper bound, in units of the Find-Any reference scale. The authors evaluate the Gingrich–Williams–Cerf baseline in the same units and divide its coefficient by the verified one. For $m=k=2$, the reported comparison is about $0.942/0.81831\approx1.15$.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.groverFindAnyRelCost
lean.annotation: The bound uses the same rational at every grid point. The best reported ratio in the interior occurs at $m=1024$, where the manuscript compares approximately $0.997$ for GW with $0.818310$ for the verified upper bound. The resulting factor rounds to $1.22$.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.GroverSolution.FindAny.relCost
lean.annotation: For an initial Grover angle $\theta$, the setup approaches $\pi/4$ in about $\pi/(8\theta)$ rounds. The calibrated check has click probability asymptotic to $4\theta$, so waiting adds about $1/(4\theta)$ rounds. With $\theta\sim\sqrt{mk/N}$, normalization by Eq. (7) gives $1/2+1/\pi$. Lean proves a rational upper bound slightly above this coefficient.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.GroverSolution.FindAny.relCost
lean.annotation: GW applies Grover rotations separately to $m$ copies of the full-domain state and combines their success probabilities at readout. The joint circuit has an odd-parity fraction asymptotic to $mk/N$, so its leading Grover angle is larger by a factor of $\sqrt m$. The weak-loop proof gives one normalized bound across the grid.
